title: The Postcards of the coast road
premise: Wren Zhou, once a piano prodigy who vanished from the conservatory at nineteen, returns a decade later as a janitor, hiding behind a practiced smile. When the coastal house where he grew up — and where his mother died under circumstances he has never explained — goes up for auction, he discovers the buyer is Daniel Reyes, the boy who witnessed everything that summer and whose testimony destroyed Wren's family. As Wren sorts through his mother's postcards, each addressed to a stranger he cannot forgive, he uncovers the truth: she chose to take the blame for a crime committed by the man everyone loved, to protect Wren's future. In the end, Wren must decide whether exposing that truth will free him or simply transfer the price of survival onto someone new; he forgives Daniel, lets the house go, and plays again — not for an audience, but at last for himself.
about_author: Edmund Vane is the pen name of a former conservatory librarian who spent fifteen years cataloguing other people's unfinished symphonies before writing his own. He lives near a coast road and collects postcards he never sends.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Introduce him mopping the conservatory halls at dawn, recognized by a former classmate now on faculty, deflecting pity with his perfected smile. Emotional beat: shame worn as armor.

chapters.title: Lot 47
chapters.summary: Wren learns the coastal house of his childhood is up for auction after the estate sale of its late owner, Aunt Mei. POV Wren. Beat: dread disguised as indifference as he decides to attend.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bids Against Me
chapters.summary: At the auction, Wren comes face to face with Daniel Reyes, now a lawyer, bidding calmly for the house. POV Wren. Beat: old rage resurfacing; Daniel wins the house.

chapters.title: Postcards, Undelivered
chapters.summary: Sorting his mother's belongings in a storage unit, Wren finds forty postcards she wrote but never mailed, all addressed to someone named only 'R.' POV Wren. Beat: grief sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Daniel's Version
chapters.summary: POV shift to Daniel, unpacking boxes in the house, haunted by the summer he testified at fourteen and what his father made him say. Beat: guilt he has never named aloud.

chapters.title: The Conservatory Recital
chapters.summary: Wren is assigned to clean after a student recital; hearing a Chopin nocturne he once performed, his hands shake. POV Wren. Beat: the past demanding reentry.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Daniel finds Wren standing outside the auctioned house at dusk; instead of confrontation, they share an awkward, charged silence about the sea. Alternating POV. Beat: enemies circling, neither leaving.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Remember
chapters.summary: Wren interviews elderly neighbors about the night his mother was arrested, collecting contradictions. POV Wren. Beat: the official story beginning to crack.

chapters.title: R Is for Ruth
chapters.summary: Wren identifies 'R' as Ruth Calloway, his mother's closest friend, now in a care home, who refuses to speak unless he brings the postcards. POV Wren. Beat: hope entangled with fear.

chapters.title: Daniel's Father's House
chapters.summary: Daniel confronts his dying father about that summer and receives a deflection that confirms something was buried. POV Daniel. Beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The First Postcard
chapters.summary: Ruth reads the first postcard aloud: an apology dated three days before the arrest. POV Wren. Beat: vertigo — his mother knew what was coming.

chapters.title: Practice Rooms
chapters.summary: Wren secretly plays an abandoned practice room at night; a student hears him and spreads word that the ghost prodigy has returned. POV Wren. Beat: tentative resurrection of the self he buried.

chapters.title: Dinner With the Enemy
chapters.summary: Daniel invites Wren to the house; over his mother's old recipes they circle the truth without touching it. Alternating POV. Beat: unexpected tenderness between adversaries.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ruth reveals the shape of it: Wren's mother took responsibility for a hit-and-run committed by Daniel's father, to shield fourteen-year-old Wren from losing both parents. POV Wren. Beat: the world inverting.

chapters.title: Evidence, Fading
chapters.summary: Daniel searches his father's papers and finds the repaired car's records, proof that could reopen everything — or destroy two families twice. POV Daniel. Beat: duty versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Auction of Memory
chapters.summary: Wren, offered a chance to buy back the house cheaply if he stays silent, must weigh home against justice. POV Wren. Beat: temptation wearing the face of mercy.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: On the beach below the house, Daniel confesses his testimony was coached; Wren confesses he has hated the wrong person for ten years. Alternating POV. Beat: love arriving exactly where hatred lived.

chapters.title: What Justice Wants
chapters.summary: Wren takes the evidence to a journalist; the case threatens to explode just as his father, estranged and ill, asks to see him. POV Wren. Beat: justice revealed as a cost, not a cure.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Daniel's father, lucid at last, admits everything privately to his son but begs him to let the dead stay dead. POV Daniel. Beat: the full weight of inherited silence.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Days
chapters.summary: With the statute deadline and the story going to press, Wren and Daniel race to decide how much truth the living can carry. Alternating POV. Beat: rising tension toward irrevocable choice.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Postcards
chapters.summary: Climax: at a small public gathering at the old house, Wren reads all forty postcards aloud, letting his mother's voice finally testify; the town must hear what love cost her. POV Wren. Beat: catharsis, exposure, forgiveness begun.

chapters.title: Coda, in C Minor
chapters.summary: Resolution: the case settles quietly, the house becomes a music school, and Wren gives one public performance — then walks the coast road at dawn, lighter, unburdened, smiling for real. POV Wren. Beat: peace earned, not granted.
